title: Dealing with Duplicates 👯
description: Identify and remove duplicate rows to keep your analysis accurate.

slides.title: Why Duplicates Matter 👥
slides.content:
# Duplicate Data = Distorted Insights

Duplicates can arise from:
- Repeated data entry
- Merging datasets that share records
- System errors

Counting sums, averages, etc. on duplicated rows inflates results. Pandas gives you tools to detect and remove them.

slides.title: Create a DataFrame with Duplicates
slides.codeSnippet:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame({
    'Name': ['Alice', 'Bob', 'Alice', 'Bob', 'Charlie'],
    'Score': [85, 92, 85, 92, 78],
    'Age': [25, 30, 25, 30, 35]
})
print(df)

slides.title: Identifying Duplicates 🔍
slides.content:
## `duplicated()`

Returns a Boolean Series indicating whether a row is a duplicate of a previous row.

- `df.duplicated()` – marks all duplicates (first occurrence is `False`).
- `df.duplicated(keep='last')` – marks duplicates except the last.
- `df.duplicated(keep=False)` – marks all duplicate rows as `True`.

```python
print(df.duplicated())
```

slides.title: Detect Duplicates
slides.content: Run to see which rows are duplicated:
slides.codeSnippet:
print('Duplicate mask:')
print(df.duplicated())
print('\nRows that are duplicates:')
print(df[df.duplicated(keep=False)])

quizData.question: What does `df.duplicated(keep='last')` mark as True?

options.text: All rows except the last duplicate
All rows except the first duplicate

quizData.explanation: With `keep='last'`, the last occurrence is considered unique, earlier duplicates are marked True.

slides.title: Removing Duplicates 🗑️
slides.content:
## `drop_duplicates()`

Removes duplicate rows. Same `keep` options as `duplicated()`.

- `df.drop_duplicates()` – keeps first occurrence.
- `df.drop_duplicates(keep='last')` – keeps last.
- `df.drop_duplicates(keep=False)` – drops all duplicates entirely.

```python
df_unique = df.drop_duplicates()
```

You can also specify a subset of columns to consider: `df.drop_duplicates(subset=['Name'])`.

quizData.question: If you run `df.drop_duplicates(subset=['Name'])`, which rows remain?

options.text: First occurrence of each unique name
Only rows with unique names across all columns
Rows where Name is not duplicated

quizData.explanation: When subset is specified, only that column is considered for duplicate detection. The first row for each name is kept.

slides.title: Caution ⚠️
slides.content:
## Resetting Index After Removal

After dropping duplicates, the index may be non‑contiguous. Use `df.reset_index(drop=True)` to get a clean integer index.

```python
df_clean = df.drop_duplicates().reset_index(drop=True)
```

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Check for Exact Duplicate Rows

`df[df.duplicated()]` shows the rows that are duplicates. Always inspect them before dropping!

slides.title: Duplicate Cleanup 🏋️
slides.content:
1. Create a DataFrame with columns `['ID','Name','Score']` and include some duplicate rows (same ID and Name, maybe different Score).
2. Print rows that are duplicated based on all columns.
3. Drop duplicates based only on `ID` and `Name` (keeping the first occurrence).
4. Reset the index and print the final DataFrame.

slides.title: Duplicates Done! 🎉
slides.content: Your data is now unique. Next, we'll fix mismatched types.
